title: I'm confused: AI will likely help indie devs develop games 10x faster, especially in 10-15 years, so why do people hate AI gamedev?
author: Ok_Nerve8120
selftext:
Sounds like stupid traditionalism to me.

Emphasis on veteran, but you can just be intermediate to advanced and that's fine. Here I'm not even speaking about art for final releases, leaving that aside since its a sensitive topic, but I'm more so speaking about people that know what they are doing, know how to code, could easily make the game themselves, but in like, 10 or 15 years, or even now, would be able to develop their game in a fraction of the time thanks to AI assisted coding and placeholder assets for the art.

Its kinda like using Wix to make a website, but drastically different, though thats one of the few examples that come to mind. You, as an Indie dev team, or single developer, should be happy about this, no? Like, you get to do things way faster and put even more time into polishing your game.

I do agree a bunch of AI slop games full of bugs on the market sounds fucking annoying, actually well made games where the dev's vision is just expedited by AI, you're just getting more, better quality products, sooner.

Why hate AI then? Its hella confusing for me. Its like being a mangaka/comic book artist/animator and hating on digital art, like, you can just transition and draw faster, with more freedom, comfort, convenience and get more free time to do whatever you want.

AI is on track to aid intermediate, advanced and veteran gamedevs turn what would be a 10 year project into a 3 year project, while maintaining the same quality. To the point you can put even more years in if its your life's work and make it better than it'd ever be in less time. Assuming a 10-15 year time gap from now.
